note: Paraphrased interviewer prompts labeled with acceptable Best Answer questionIds. Written by hand to differ from canonical wording; replace or extend with prompts heard in real Teams mocks. Negatives have no reliable Best Answer and should come back not confident.

positives.query: What was the best internship you've had so far, and what made it great?
Which of your past internships did you enjoy the most?
In your view, what separates a great product from a mediocre one?
What qualities make a PM successful?
What does a great product manager do differently from an average one?
Tell me about an app you use every day. What do you love about it and what would you change?
Tell me about a time you had to resolve a disagreement within your team.
Describe a situation where two teams wanted different things and you had to get them on the same page.
What would your previous manager say is your biggest strength?
What's an area you're actively trying to get better at?
Which Microsoft product do you use the most, and how would you make it better?
Give me an example of when you led a team.
Tell me about a time you stepped up and rallied a group toward a goal.
If you could go back and redo one of your projects, what would you change?
Looking back at something you shipped, what would you do differently with what you know now?
How did you balance design polish against getting the core features out?
Walk me through your background.
So, tell me about yourself.
Why are you interested in this PM internship at Microsoft?
You mentioned an 8% lift in generation starts. What exactly was the numerator and the denominator?
Pick a number on your resume and explain exactly how it was calculated and validated.
Tell me about something you built from zero with no existing playbook.
Walk me through the most technically complex thing you've built.
What APIs have you integrated, and what did they let the product do?
Tell me about a time something you tried didn't work out.
Tell me about a mistake you made at work and what you learned from it.
How do you decide what to cut when you don't have enough engineering time?
How did you figure out what users actually needed before deciding what to build?

How would you explain a complicated recommendation to someone who isn't technical?
How do you handle it when priorities keep shifting under you?
Tell me about a time you received tough feedback.
Describe a creative solution you came up with that others hadn't considered.
Tell me about a process you streamlined or automated.
Tell me about a risk you took on a project and how you limited the downside.
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision but committed to it anyway.
Have you ever had to choose between shipping fast and doing it right?
Why product management instead of staying in data science?
You're joining a brand new team next week. What do you do in your first month?
Two weeks before launch, engineering tells you the feature can't be built. What do you do?
Your VP wants to go in a direction the user research doesn't support. How do you handle that?
There's a critical issue that falls between two teams and no one is picking it up. What would you do?
Tell me about a time you went above and beyond your job description.
How have you used AI tools in your work, and how do you make sure the output is correct?
Explain one technical concept from your work as if I were a non-technical executive.
How do you work with engineers and designers day to day?
Who was on that team, and how did you divide up the work?
Tell me about a time data changed your mind.
Give an example of an experiment whose result changed what you recommended.
About the Three.js homepage idea: what exactly was the disagreement and what got rejected?
What's a product you really like, and what's one thing you'd fix about it?
